result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers open by calling the set sound, then pile on many new tokens and scales the team didn't ask for, which goes against the rubric's preference for few, targeted changes. A is noticeably shorter and suggests fewer additions. B goes further, adding info, on-status, raised and sunken surfaces, border-width and longer-duration tokens, though it hedges its contrast numbers more consistently. A's tighter scope makes it the better sanity pass, even though it states 'contrast is solid' as fact before admitting the ratios were estimated by hand. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers turn a sanity pass into a long list of new tokens, which goes against the rubric's preference for few, justified changes. B opens with a clearer verdict ('in good shape'), keeps only four must-fix items, and is somewhat shorter, though it states that contrast passes before hedging later. A has more numbered fixes and more speculative additions (on-* pairs, info, raised and sunken surfaces, border widths, a longer duration), even though its contrast caveats are more consistent.
